player.title: Player Guide
player.subtitle: How to apply for a minister slot, step by step.
player.whatIsBody: On the SVS prep days the state gives minister positions to players in 30-minute slots. You tell us your speedups and the hours you can be online. The leaders then give the slots to the biggest contributors first, at the hours they picked.
player.step1Fid: On the minister page, press "Apply or update". Enter your player ID (FID) and press Next. Can't find it? Tap "Where do I find my player ID?": in the game, tap your profile picture (top left); the number under your name is your ID.
player.step1Speedups: Enter your speedups in DAYS for Construction, Research and Troop Training. If the leaders turned them on, also enter your Fire Crystals, Refined Fire Crystals and Fire Crystal Shards.
player.step1General: Planning to use General speedups for Construction or Research? Add those days to the Construction or Research totals.
player.step2Select: There is one step for each SVS day: Construction (Monday), Research (Tuesday or Friday) and Troop Training (Thursday).
player.step2Days: Tap ALL the hours you can be online. The more hours you pick, the better your chance of getting a slot.
player.step2Timezone: Each hour shows your own time and the game time (UTC). Use the timezone menu on the step to change your time zone.
player.step2Tolerance: Your real slot may be up to 20 minutes before or after the hour you picked (e.g. 05:00 can become 04:50 or 05:20).
player.step3Body: Check everything, then press Submit (or Update when you are changing your application).
player.heatmapBody: The colour of each hour shows how many other players picked it:
player.heatmapTip: Tip: if you can, also pick some blue (quiet) hours: they are easier to get.
player.updateBody1: On the minister page, press "Apply or update":
player.updateStep1: Enter the same player ID on step 1 and press Next.
player.updateStep2: If the leaders have published a schedule, your slots are shown at the top. If not, it says you have not been assigned yet.
player.updateStep3: Your saved answers are already filled in. Go through the steps and change what you need.
player.updateStep4: Press "Update" on the last step to save.
player.updateNote: Slots can still change until they are confirmed in the game. Check again before the day.
player.assignmentsBody: How the leaders' tool decides who gets which slot:
player.assignmentsPoint1: Your speedups (and fire crystals, when asked) give you points for each day. More points = higher priority.
player.assignmentsPoint2: Each day is cut into 30-minute slots.
player.assignmentsPoint3: Players with the most points get their chosen hours first.
player.assignmentsPoint4: If all your hours are taken by players with more points, you may be left without a slot. The leaders can still move you by hand.
player.timezoneBody: The game runs on UTC. The clock at the top of every page picks the time zone used to show times. It starts with your phone's time zone and remembers your choice. Example: 05:00 UTC is 08:00 if you are in UTC+3.
player.tip1: Pick every hour you can really be online: being flexible helps the most.
player.tip2: Enter your speedups honestly. Bigger numbers don't help: leaders can check.
player.tip3: Look at the colours: blue hours are less crowded.
player.tip4: After the leaders publish, check "View Published Schedule" for your slot.
player.tip5: If your plans change, update your application straight away, not at the last minute.
player.roundsNote: Each minister round (one SVS week) is a new application. Your name, alliance and furnace are remembered, but speedups and hours start blank. Press "Use my last answers" to copy them from your last round.
player.step1Profile: Check your in-game name and alliance tag (needed, up to 3 letters). If you applied before, they are already filled in. Wrong player? Tap "Not you? Use a different FID".
player.step1Furnace: Furnace level is optional. Pick it from the list: FC10 down to FC1 first, then 30 down to 1 for furnaces before Fire Crystal.
player.step2Empty: Can't play on one of the days? Pick no hours and confirm when you are asked.
player.deadline1: The minister page shows when applications close, in your own time zone.
player.deadline2: After that, new players can't apply. If you already applied, you can still change your answers.
player.schedule1: When the leaders publish a day, a "View Published Schedule" button appears on the minister page.
player.schedule2: It shows who has each slot that day.
player.schedule3: Your own slots are also shown at the top of step 1 when you open "Apply or update" with your player ID.

tyrantPlayer.title: Frost Dragon Tyrant guide
tyrantPlayer.subtitle: How to sign up for the Frost Dragon Tyrant fight, step by step.
tyrantPlayer.whatIsBody: Before each Frost Dragon Tyrant event the leaders need to know who can fight, when, and how strong each troop type is. Your sign-up helps them choose rally leaders and joiners for each time window.
tyrantPlayer.roundsNote: Each Tyrant event is a new sign-up. Your name, alliance, Discord ID, power and troops are remembered; time windows, gems and roles start blank. Press "Use my last answers" to copy them from your last sign-up.
tyrantPlayer.open: On the Frost Dragon Tyrant page, press "Sign up or update". Then:
tyrantPlayer.s1: Player Identity: enter your player ID (FID) and press Next. Tap "Where do I find my player ID?" if you need help. Check your in-game name and alliance (both needed). Discord ID is optional.
tyrantPlayer.s2: Availability: tap every time window you can attend, or "Select All Time Slots". "Opening Rush" is the start of the fight. Tick "Can listen in Discord VC" if you can listen to voice chat.
tyrantPlayer.s3: Player Stats: your power in millions (e.g. 410) and the most gems you would spend. Both are optional.
tyrantPlayer.s4: Troop Levels: for Infantry, Lancer and Marksman pick the CAMP level (FC1 to FC10) and your troop tier (T8 to T11). All six are needed.
tyrantPlayer.s5: Roles Wanted: tick what you would like to do: Rally Leader, Joiner, Gathering/Looting, Battle Management or Event Preparation.
tyrantPlayer.s6: Review Your Info: check everything (each part has an Edit button), then press Submit.
tyrantPlayer.campsTitle: Why we ask for camp levels
tyrantPlayer.camps1: Each troop type trains in its own camp, and a camp can be lower than your furnace. Example: an FC9 furnace with an FC7 Infantry Camp.
tyrantPlayer.camps2: Your troops are only as strong as their camp. Pick each camp's own level, not your furnace level.
tyrantPlayer.camps3: Leaders use camp level + tier to find the strongest joiners. The best joiner has FC10 camps and T11 troops.
tyrantPlayer.camps4: Your camp levels and tiers are also used for the SVS sign-up, so keep them up to date.
tyrantPlayer.times1: Time windows are game time (UTC): the time the event runs on.
tyrantPlayer.times2: Other times, like when sign-ups close, are shown in your own time zone. Change it with the clock at the top.
tyrantPlayer.edit1: Press "Sign up or update" again and enter the same player ID. Your saved answers are filled in.
tyrantPlayer.edit2: Change what you need and press Update on the last step.
tyrantPlayer.edit3: For the next Tyrant event you make a new sign-up ("Use my last answers" saves typing).
tyrantPlayer.deadline1: The page shows when sign-ups close. After that, new players can't sign up, but you can still change your sign-up.
tyrantPlayer.deadline2: If the page says sign-ups are not open, there is no event right now. Check back later or ask your leaders.
tyrantPlayer.tip1: Be honest about camps and tiers: leaders plan the rallies around them.
tyrantPlayer.tip2: Pick every window you can really attend.
tyrantPlayer.tip3: If you see "Too many requests", wait a minute and try again.

svsPlayer.title: SVS Castle guide
svsPlayer.subtitle: How to sign up for the castle battle, and how to read the battle plan.
svsPlayer.whatIsBody: In State vs State the castle battle needs a plan: who leads rallies, who joins whom, and with which heroes. Your sign-up tells the leaders when you can fight and how strong your troops are. They build the plan and share it with the state.
svsPlayer.roundsNote: Each SVS is a new sign-up. Your name, alliance and troops are remembered; hours and voice chat start blank. Press "Use my last answers" to copy them.
svsPlayer.open: On the SVS Castle page, press "Sign up or update". Then:
svsPlayer.s1: Player: enter your player ID (FID) and press Next. Check your in-game name. New players also give their 3-letter alliance tag; others change it only if they moved.
svsPlayer.s2: Battle hours: tap every hour of the battle you will be online, or "I can do every hour". The big time is game time (UTC); the small time under it is your time.
svsPlayer.s3: Troops: for Infantry, Lancer and Marksman pick the camp's FC level and your troop tier (T10 or T11).
svsPlayer.s4: Voice chat: say if you can join Discord voice chat. Listening is enough.
svsPlayer.s5: Review: check everything and press Submit.
svsPlayer.troops1: Pick each camp's own level: a camp can be lower than your furnace.
svsPlayer.troops2: SVS only counts T10 and T11. If you saved T8 or T9 for Frost Dragon Tyrant, pick T10 or T11 here.
svsPlayer.troops3: Troops are shared with Frost Dragon Tyrant: update them in one place and the other is ready.
svsPlayer.leaders1: There is no role question. The leaders choose the rally leaders and the joiners themselves when they make the battle plan.
svsPlayer.leaders2: Strong camps and tiers, more hours and voice chat make you easier to place.
svsPlayer.edit1: Press "Sign up or update" again with the same player ID, change what you need and press Update.
svsPlayer.edit2: The page shows when sign-ups close. After that, new players can't sign up, but you can still change yours.
svsPlayer.planIntro: Your leaders send you a secret link to the plan. It is read-only, made for phones and always shows the latest version: open it again just before the battle.
svsPlayer.planFind: Find me: type your in-game name or player ID and press Find. The page jumps to your place and says it in a sentence, e.g. "You are joiner 2 of Rally Caller 01".
svsPlayer.planGroups: Groups: Main (and Counter, when two alliances fight) hold the rallies. An extra group (e.g. Turrets) lists players with another job. A group can have notes and joining rules: the lowest camp level and tier for everyone else who joins.
svsPlayer.planLeader: Each rally leader has a number, 3 heroes, a troop ratio and a pet-buff time.
svsPlayer.planSplit: Some leaders have separate Rally and Garrison parts. Each part has its own heroes and troop ratio.
svsPlayer.planJoiners: Named joiners: lead your march with the hero shown next to your name (your 2nd and 3rd heroes don't matter). Use the leader's troop ratio, unless "Own ratio" is shown next to your name.
svsPlayer.planEveryone: "Everyone else may use": the heroes allowed for joiners who are not named. "Extra joiners" are listed by name only.
svsPlayer.planPet: Pet buffs: the leader uses them "At open", "2 hours in" or in the "Last hour". The game time is shown next to it.
svsPlayer.planTimes: Battle times are game time (UTC); your own time is shown next to them.
svsPlayer.ratioExample: Example troop ratio: 50% Infantry, 20% Lancer, 30% Marksman (always 100% in total).
svsPlayer.disguiseTitle: Aliases and disguises: keep them secret
svsPlayer.disguise1: On battle day some leaders change their profile picture to a chosen hero and their name to an alias (e.g. "Rally Caller 01"), so the enemy can't tell who is who.
svsPlayer.disguise2: The plan shows the alias and that hero's picture. The leaders can also show the real name next to it.
svsPlayer.disguise3: Never share the plan link, screenshots or who is behind an alias outside our state. If the link leaks, tell your leaders: they can replace it, and the old link stops working at once.
svsPlayer.disguise4: If the link says it doesn't work, it was replaced or turned off. Ask your leaders for the new link.
svsPlayer.tip1: Sign up early, even if you can only do one hour.
svsPlayer.tip2: Join voice chat if you can: leaders call the timing there.
svsPlayer.tip3: Check the plan again just before the battle: it can change.

basics.title: Event Management basics
basics.hint: Logging in, rounds, closing times, Add player, exports and links work the same in every event: see "Event Management basics".
basics.subtitle: What works the same in every event: logging in, rounds, closing times, adding players, exports and links.
basics.login1: Open Event Management with the small link at the bottom of an event page, and enter the admin password. You land on that event's dashboard.
basics.login2: Use the event switch at the top to move between events without logging in again.
basics.login3: Press Logout when you are done, especially on a shared device. A login lasts up to 12 hours; then you are asked to log in again.
basics.login4: After several wrong passwords, logins are slowed down ("Too many attempts"). Wait a little and try again.
basics.roundsBody: Every event happens again and again. Each time is a round, with its own sign-ups and settings. Player profiles (name, alliance, troops) stay from round to round.
basics.rounds1: Open: the current round. Players can sign up and edit. Only one round per event can be open.
basics.rounds2: Draft: prepared but not open to players.
basics.rounds3: Closed: a past round. You can look at it and export it, but nothing can be changed (read-only).
basics.rounds4: The Round menu at the top chooses the round you look at. It shows each round's status and number of sign-ups.
basics.start1: Press "Start new round", type a name (a dated name is suggested) and, if you like, a closing time.
basics.start2: The current round closes and the new one opens. Nothing is deleted.
basics.start3: The new round copies the settings of the last one (time windows, battle hours, research day and so on).
basics.start4: Players then make a new sign-up. "Use my last answers" copies their answers from the round before.
basics.rename1: Press "Rename" next to the Round menu to change a round's name. It works on every round, closed ones too.
basics.closing1: Set a closing time on the event's Settings tab, or when you start a round. Press Clear to remove it.
basics.closing2: Type it in your display time zone: the clock at the top of the page. The field says which zone it uses.
basics.closing3: After the closing time, new players can't sign up, but players who already did can still edit. To stop all changes, start a new round.
basics.closing4: Players see the closing time in their own time zone.
basics.add1: For players who didn't sign up themselves: press "Add player", enter their player ID and press "Look up".
basics.add2: For a known player the name, alliance and troops are filled in. For a new ID, type their in-game name.
basics.add3: Everything else is optional. The player can complete it later with their player ID.
basics.add4: If the player already has a sign-up in this round, you are asked to edit that one instead.
basics.export1: In Frost Dragon Tyrant and SVS the filters are saved in the page address: bookmark it or send it to another admin.
basics.export2: CSV and Excel exports only include the players that match the current filters. Clear the filters to export everyone.
basics.export3: Exports use each player's current profile (name, alliance, troops).
basics.state1: State Number (Minister → Settings) shows "Welcome, State #…" on every event page. Leave it empty to hide that line.
basics.state2: State hero generation (Minister → Settings, or SVS → Heroes) is the newest hero generation your state has. The battle planner only offers heroes up to it. It counts for the whole state.
basics.links1: For state chat: the event pages /minister, /tyrant and /svs on this site. Each has a "How does it work?" guide for players.
basics.links2: For admins: /admin opens Event Management on the event you used last. Add ?event=tyrant or ?event=svs to open that event.
basics.links3: The SVS battle plan has its own secret link (Battle plan → Share). Share it only inside the state.
basics.limits1: To stop abuse, player ID look-ups and sign-ups are limited per internet connection (about 30 look-ups and 10 sign-ups a minute).
basics.limits2: A player who hits the limit sees "Too many requests in a short time". Many players on one Wi-Fi can hit it together: ask them to wait a minute and try again.
basics.limits3: Admin pages have no limit, except the login (see above).

admin.title: Admin Guide
admin.subtitle: How to run Minister applications: players, assignments, settings and publishing.
admin.overviewBody: The Minister admin has three tabs. Players: the applications of the selected round (search, sort, edit, delete, add, export and import). Assignments: auto-assign each day's slots, fix them by hand, lock them and publish. Settings: the state number and hero generation (for the whole state), then this round's closing time, research day, fire crystals, time slot scheme and published days.
admin.playersView1: The table lists every application in the round: name and alliance, player ID, the points for each day and how many hours they picked.
admin.playersView2: Click a column header to sort (e.g. Monday points to see the top contributors). Click again to reverse.
admin.playersView3: Use the search bar to find a player by name or player ID.
admin.playersView4: Points come from the speedups for each day, plus fire crystals when they are switched on in Settings.
admin.playersEdit1: Press Edit on a row to change an application.
admin.playersEdit2: You can change the name, alliance, furnace level, speedups and hours.
admin.playersEdit3: Press Save. The points are worked out again.
admin.playersDeleteBody: Delete removes the application (and its assignments) from this round, after you confirm. The player profile is kept. To start over for the next SVS, use "Start new round" instead: nothing is deleted and past rounds stay viewable.
admin.exportBody: "Export Players" downloads the applications of this round as a JSON file: a backup with speedups and hours.
admin.importBody: "Import Players" reads such a file into the selected round. Players are matched by player ID: existing ones are updated, new ones are added.
admin.autoAssign1: On the Assignments tab pick a day (Monday, Tuesday or Friday, Thursday) and press "Auto Assign".
admin.autoAssign2: Players with the most points for that day get their chosen hours first.
admin.autoAssign3: Each 30-minute slot gets one player. Players who don't fit are listed under "Unassigned Players".
admin.autoAssign4: You can run it again at any time: locked players are not moved.
admin.dragDrop1: Drag a player card to another slot to move them.
admin.dragDrop2: Drag a player to "Unassigned Players" to take them off the schedule.
admin.sticky1: A player you place by hand is locked automatically (lock icon).
admin.sticky2: Locked players stay where they are when you run Auto Assign again.
admin.sticky3: Click the lock icon to lock or unlock a player.
admin.sticky4: Lock the key players first, then let Auto Assign fill the rest.
admin.settingsBody: First the settings for the whole state, then the selected round's own settings (a new round starts with a copy):
admin.settingsState: State Number: shown as "Welcome, State #…" on every event page.
admin.settingsClosing: Application Closing Time: typed in your display time zone. After it, new players can't apply, but those who did can still update. The minister page shows the time, then "Applications are now closed."
admin.settingsResearch: Research day: Tuesday or Friday, as your state's SVS runs. It changes the day name and which hours are used for research.
admin.settingsFireCrystals: Show Fire Crystal fields: asks players for Fire Crystals, Refined Fire Crystals and Shards, which add to their points.
admin.publishBody: When a day's assignments are ready, publish it so players can see it:
admin.publish1: Press "Publish Schedule" on each day you want to show.
admin.publish2: Published days get a "View Published Schedule" button on the minister page.
admin.publish3: Press "Unpublish" to hide a day again while you make changes.
admin.excelBody: "Export to Excel" downloads all the assignments of the round:
admin.excel1: One sheet per day (Monday, Tuesday or Friday, Thursday) plus an "Unassigned" sheet.
admin.excel2: Each sheet shows the slots, player names, alliances and points.
admin.excel3: Use it for your records or to share with leaders who have no admin access.
admin.workflow1: Start a new round and set the closing time (and research day) in Settings.
admin.workflow2: Share the minister page in state chat and wait for applications.
admin.workflow3: Check the Players tab for odd numbers or missing details; add players who couldn't apply.
admin.workflow4: On the Assignments tab, run Auto Assign for each day.
admin.workflow5: Fix problems by hand (drag-and-drop or Move here).
admin.workflow6: Lock the placements you want to keep.
admin.workflow7: Export to Excel for your records.
admin.workflow8: Publish each day when it's ready: players then see it on the minister page.
admin.addBody: "Add player" creates an application for someone who didn't apply (see Event Management basics). Their speedups and hours can stay empty: fill them in later with Edit.
admin.dragDrop4: On a phone: tap the move icon on a player, then "Move here" (or "Swap here") on a slot. A long press also starts a drag.
admin.settingsHeroes: State hero generation: the newest hero generation your state has (used by the SVS battle planner).
admin.settingsScheme: Time Slot Scheme: Exact Alignment (00:00, 00:30 … 48 slots a day) or Maximum Slots (starts 23:50 the night before, 49 slots). Switching moves existing assignments to the nearest new slot.
admin.settingsPublished: Published schedule days: the same switch as Publish / Unpublish on the Assignments tab.
admin.publish4: Players also see their own published slots at the top of the application when they open it with their player ID.

tyrantAdmin.subtitle: How to run Frost Dragon Tyrant sign-ups: rounds, time windows, stats, filters and exports.
tyrantAdmin.overviewBody: The Frost Dragon Tyrant admin has two tabs. Players: the sign-ups of the selected round, with stats, breakdowns, filters, a sortable table, exports, Add player and delete. Settings: the round's time windows and closing time. Tyrant doesn't ask for the furnace level: each troop camp's level and tier show how strong a player is.
tyrantAdmin.rounds1: Each Tyrant event is a round. The Round menu shows the current round; pick an older one to look back.
tyrantAdmin.rounds2: "Start new round" closes the current round and opens a new one with the name you choose (and an optional closing time). Nothing is deleted.
tyrantAdmin.rounds3: The new round copies the time windows of the last one. Players make a new sign-up and can press "Use my last answers".
tyrantAdmin.rounds4: Past rounds are read-only: you can view and export them, but not change them.
tyrantAdmin.windowsBody: On the Settings tab you set the time windows (UTC) that players can pick in this round:
tyrantAdmin.windows1: Change a window's start and end time; the end must be after the start.
tyrantAdmin.windows2: Tick "Opening Rush" on the windows that count as the opening rush (shown first, with their time).
tyrantAdmin.windows3: Add a window (up to 12) or remove one. "Reset to defaults" brings back the standard windows from 11:01 to 18:00.
tyrantAdmin.windows4: Press "Save windows" to apply. Changes affect this round only; players who already chose a removed window keep it on their sign-up.
tyrantAdmin.closingBody: Set a closing time on the Settings tab (or when you start a round), in your display time zone. After it, new players can't sign up, but players who already did can still edit. Press Clear to remove it.
tyrantAdmin.statsBody: The top of the Players tab sums up the round:
tyrantAdmin.stats1: Cards: total players ("of N" when filtered), players for the opening rush, Discord VC and the number of alliances. There is no gem total: each player's gems are in the table.
tyrantAdmin.stats2: Troops: for each troop type, how many players have each camp level (FC10 … FC1, old pre-FC values as stored, none) and each tier (T11 … T8, none). Then players per time window, roles wanted and alliances.
tyrantAdmin.stats3: Every count and bar is a button: tap it to filter by it, tap again to remove the filter. Several combine. All stats are worked out again for the filtered players.
tyrantAdmin.filters1: Search by in-game name, player ID or Discord ID.
tyrantAdmin.filters2: The filter bar: alliance (several allowed), time windows or "Opening Rush", troop type (or all three) with "Camp at least" and tier (T10 or better / T11 only). "More filters" adds Discord VC, power, gems, roles (any or all) and the sign-up date.
tyrantAdmin.filters3: Click a column header to sort; click again to reverse.
tyrantAdmin.filters4: Big rounds are split into pages: use Previous and Next.
tyrantAdmin.exportBody: Download the sign-ups of the selected round:
tyrantAdmin.export1: Export CSV: one row per player, for spreadsheets or bots.
tyrantAdmin.export2: Export Excel: a formatted sheet plus a Summary sheet. Both use each player's current profile (name, alliance, camp levels, tiers) and only include the players that match the current filters.
tyrantAdmin.deleteBody: The delete button on a row removes a duplicate or test sign-up (you are asked to confirm). It only removes the sign-up from this round; the player profile is kept. Past rounds can't be changed.
tyrantAdmin.workflow1: Start a new round and set a closing time.
tyrantAdmin.workflow2: Check the time windows on the Settings tab and save them.
tyrantAdmin.workflow3: Share the Frost Dragon Tyrant page in state chat.
tyrantAdmin.workflow4: Watch the stats as sign-ups arrive; remove duplicates and add players who couldn't sign up.
tyrantAdmin.workflow5: After the closing time, filter and sort (e.g. by Strength) to plan rallies, then export to CSV or Excel.
tyrantAdmin.workflow6: Before the next Tyrant event, start a new round: this one stays as history.
tyrantAdmin.filters5: Filters combine (all must match). Each active filter is a pill: tap it to remove it, or "Clear filters" to remove all. Filters are kept in the page address, so you can bookmark or share a filtered view.
tyrantAdmin.filters6: Strength (sortable) ranks joiners: for each troop type the camp's FC number plus the tier, added up (FC10 camps with T11 everywhere = 63).
tyrantAdmin.addBody: "Add player" signs up someone who didn't do it themselves. Only the player ID and in-game name are needed; time windows, Discord VC, troops (T8–T11) and roles are optional.

svsAdmin.subtitle: How to run SVS: sign-ups, battle hours, stats, exports, heroes and the battle plan.
svsAdmin.overviewBody: The SVS admin has four tabs. Players: the sign-ups with stats, filters, the table, exports, Add player and delete. Battle plan: build the rally plan and share it. Settings: battle start, length and closing time. Heroes: the hero library and the state hero generation. Players sign up in five short steps: player, battle hours, troops (camp FC level + T10 or T11), Discord voice chat and review.
svsAdmin.rounds1: Each SVS is one round. "Start new round" closes the current one (nothing is deleted) and opens a fresh one.
svsAdmin.rounds2: Battle hours and the other settings carry over to the new round. The battle plan does not: each round starts with an empty plan.
svsAdmin.rounds3: Past rounds stay in the Round menu. They are read-only, their plan too.
svsAdmin.battleBody: Settings tab: when the battle starts (UTC) and how many hours it lasts. The default is 11:00 UTC for 5 hours (11:00 to 16:00).
svsAdmin.battle1: Players see one button per hour, in game time (UTC) with their own time under it.
svsAdmin.battle2: If you change the hours later, players keep the hours they already picked.
svsAdmin.signup2: Each troop camp's FC level and tier: only T10 or T11 in SVS.
svsAdmin.signup3: No role question: you choose the rally leaders yourself in the Battle plan.
svsAdmin.signup4: Discord voice chat: yes or no. The alliance is only asked of new players.
svsAdmin.statsBody: The cards show total players, average battle hours per player, players with T11 in all three troop types and Discord VC. Under them: players per hour and alliances, then camp levels and tiers per troop type. Tap any bar or count to filter by it; tap again to remove the filter.
svsAdmin.filters1: Search by name or player ID. Filter by alliance, hours (players online in ALL the chosen hours), troop type, camp level and tier.
svsAdmin.filters2: "More filters": Discord VC and when they signed up. Active filters are pills; the page address keeps them.
svsAdmin.filters3: Sort by Strength to find the strongest joiners (camp FC levels + tiers, as in Frost Dragon Tyrant).
svsAdmin.exportBody: Export CSV or Excel. Both follow the current filters, so filter first to export one alliance or one hour.
svsAdmin.addBody: For players who didn't sign up: "Add player" makes their sign-up with just the player ID and in-game name; hours, voice chat and troops are optional. If they already signed up in this round, edit that one instead.
svsAdmin.heroesBody: The Heroes tab shows the hero library the planner uses, up to the state hero generation (set it there or in Minister → Settings). Rare and epic heroes have no generation and are always included.
svsAdmin.planBody: Build the plan on a computer or tablet (a phone screen is too small). Every change saves by itself.
svsAdmin.battle3: The same start and length give the pet-buff times in the battle plan.
svsAdmin.table1: Each row: name, player ID and alliance, hours (UTC), Discord VC, a troop line (e.g. "Inf FC10 T11 · Lan FC9 T10 · Mks FC10 T11"), Strength and when they signed up.
svsAdmin.table2: Click a column header to sort. Strength = the camp FC numbers plus the tiers, added up (63 at most).
svsAdmin.table3: The delete button removes a sign-up from this round only; the player profile is kept.
svsAdmin.strategy1: Pick "Single alliance" or "Main + Counter" at the top. Going back to Single moves the Counter rally leaders into Main.
svsAdmin.strategy2: Each group has a name, an alliance tag and notes. "Add another group" adds a light group (e.g. Turrets) with only players and notes.
svsAdmin.strategy3: "Joining rules for everyone else": the lowest camp level and tier per troop type. The shared plan shows them. Named joiners below them get a "Below minimum" warning, but are never blocked.
svsAdmin.leaders1: Press "Add rally leader" and search a name, player ID or alliance, or drag a sign-up from the side panel onto a group. There is no limit.
svsAdmin.leaders2: Drag the handle to change the order or move a leader to the other group. The ⋮ menu has Move to, Move up, Move down and Delete.
svsAdmin.leaders3: Choose 3 heroes and the troop ratio (Infantry / Lancer / Marksman, 100% in total).
svsAdmin.leaders4: Pet buffs: "At open", "2 hours in" or "Last hour", with the real time from the battle settings. It is your choice per leader: nothing is spread out automatically.
svsAdmin.leaders5: "Separate rally and garrison": the same joiners get their own heroes and ratio for each side.
svsAdmin.disguise1: "Add a disguise (PFP + alias)": the hero picture and name the leader uses in the game on battle day, so the enemy can't tell who is who.
svsAdmin.disguise2: Share → "Show real names to the state" (on by default) also shows the real name next to the alias on the shared page. It never changes anything in the game.
svsAdmin.joiners1: Named joiners (up to 4 per leader): pick a player and the hero they lead with. They use the leader's ratio unless you set their own troop ratio.
svsAdmin.joiners2: "Everyone else may use": up to 4 heroes allowed for all other joiners.
svsAdmin.joiners3: Extra joiners (up to 14): names only, no heroes.
svsAdmin.joiners4: A player can be in the plan only once. Search shows where someone already is (e.g. "Already with …"); press "Move here" to move them.
svsAdmin.joiners5: Quick add, for someone who didn't sign up: with a player ID they also get an SVS sign-up; without one they stay in the plan only, marked "Not signed up".
svsAdmin.heroPick1: Drag a hero from the Heroes panel onto a slot, or click a slot and then a hero. × empties a slot.
svsAdmin.heroPick2: Only heroes up to the state hero generation are offered (plus rare and epic). A hero already chosen above it stays, with a warning.
svsAdmin.save1: Every change saves by itself after a moment ("Saved · just now").
svsAdmin.save2: If someone else saved the plan from another screen, you see "Someone else changed this plan": your last change was NOT saved. Press "Reload the plan" and do it again.
svsAdmin.save3: If a save fails, your next change or "Try again" saves it.
svsAdmin.save4: In a closed round the plan is read-only.
svsAdmin.share1: Press Share, then "Create share link". Copy it and post it inside the state only.
svsAdmin.share2: The link is read-only, works well on phones, has "Find me" and always shows the latest saved plan.
svsAdmin.share3: "New link" replaces the link: the old one stops working at once (use it if the link leaks). "Turn off sharing" stops it completely.
svsAdmin.share4: The shared page links to the SVS player guide, which explains how to read the plan.
svsAdmin.workflow1: Start a new round; check the battle hours and closing time in Settings.
svsAdmin.workflow2: Share the SVS page in state chat.
svsAdmin.workflow3: Watch the sign-ups; add players who couldn't sign up.
svsAdmin.workflow4: After the closing time, build the battle plan.
svsAdmin.workflow5: Share the plan link in state chat (only inside the state).
svsAdmin.workflow6: After SVS, start a new round for the next one.
